domains.backend: Request handling, APIs, databases, queues, caching.
domains.data: Transformation, parsing, serialization, pipelines, file I/O.
domains.ml: Model loading, inference, embeddings, training utilities.
domains.infra: Deployment, config management, logging, monitoring, health checks.
domains.universal: Pure utilities with no domain dependency (string ops, retry, math, date handling). If a widget could reasonably belong to two domains, it belongs here.
domains.modeling: Parametric and generative representations of physical or visual things — 3D geometry, surfaces, shapes, simulations. Widgets produce artifacts (STL, mesh, image) rather than running as services.

general_notes: Single responsibility - one widget does one thing. No global state. No project-specific code, hardcoded paths, credentials, or environment-specific values. Expose variation points as constructor parameters or function arguments - no hardcoded thresholds, colors, sizes, or behavior flags. All dependencies must be declared in widget.json tech_stack.dependencies. Widgets cannot depend on other widgets - they must be fully self-contained. If you need logic from another widget, copy it into src/ directly. Examples must run and exit cleanly with no user input, no network calls, and no external services or API keys - use fake/hardcoded data. The widget's own declared dependencies are fine and will be installed by the validator before the example runs. Do not modify library_notes - it is managed by Cartograph and will be restored on checkin.

language_notes.python: Use pytest for all tests - no unittest. Type hints required on all public functions. No __init__.py in tests/. No if __name__ == '__main__' blocks in src/ files. Imports ordered: stdlib, third-party, local. ML domain: framework-free (numpy, scikit-learn, plain Python) and API-based inference (HTTP calls to OpenAI, Anthropic, HuggingFace Inference API) work everywhere. Heavy frameworks (torch, tensorflow, jax, and similar) are allowed but must be pre-installed - Cartograph will not auto-install them. Declare them in widget.json dependencies normally; consumers must also have them installed to validate.
language_notes.javascript: Use vitest for all tests. Include a vitest config and a coverage provider (@vitest/coverage-v8 or @vitest/coverage-istanbul) in devDependencies - the validator enforces 80% coverage via CLI flags but does not inject test configuration. No console.log() in src/ files. Use named exports, not default exports. Test filename must match src filename exactly. Only test/expect/describe/vi are global - all other imports must be explicit. Plain JS: files use .js, examples run with node and exit cleanly. Frontend (DOM) testing: add 'happy-dom' to devDependencies and set environment: 'happy-dom' in your vitest config - the scaffold does this automatically for frontend widgets. Canvas/WebGL testing: add '@vitest/browser' and 'playwright' to devDependencies and configure the browser provider in your vitest config - Playwright must be installed on the system (run 'npx playwright install chromium'). React is not scaffolded by default. To use React: add react and react-dom to dependencies, rename files to .jsx, add @vitejs/plugin-react, @testing-library/react, jsdom, and esbuild to devDependencies, and configure your vitest config with the react plugin and jsdom environment. The validator auto-detects React in dependencies to use esbuild when running the example - test environment is entirely your vitest config's responsibility. Components must be PascalCase .jsx, hooks camelCase .js starting with 'use'. Components must render cleanly via react-dom/server renderToString with no browser APIs (window, document, localStorage) in the initial render path. Usage hints: you may optionally include examples/usage_hint.* with real integration code that requires a browser or app context. These are not executed by Cartograph.
language_notes.openscad: Use module for all reusable geometry — never write top-level geometry outside a module in src/. All parameters must have defaults so the module renders on its own. Tests are .scad files that call your module with different parameters — each must render to a non-empty STL without errors. No coverage requirement: passing renders is the bar. Examples must render cleanly with no user input and no external services. Dependencies (e.g. BOSL2) must be declared in widget.json but are not auto-installed — consumers must add them to their OpenSCAD library path manually.
language_notes.nim: Use std/unittest for all tests (import std/unittest, not bare import unittest). Use func for pure procedures with no side effects — only use proc when side effects are required. Mark all public symbols with * (e.g. func myFunc*(x: int): int). Use camelCase for funcs/procs/variables, PascalCase for types. Prefer stdlib imports with the std/ prefix (e.g. import std/strutils, not import strutils). No echo in src/ files. No quit() or system.quit() in src/ files. No {.importc.} or {.compile.} pragmas — C FFI makes widgets platform-dependent and unvalidatable. No {.global.} pragma — widgets must not use global mutable state. No OS-targeting when defined(windows/linux/posix/etc.) — widgets must validate on all platforms. A widget_id.nimble file is required at the widget root - it is created by cartograph create and must stay in sync with widget.json dependencies. List nimble package dependencies in widget.json tech_stack.dependencies as 'pkgname >= version'.

domain_notes.backend: Every tunable should be a parameter: timeouts, retry counts, pool sizes, base URLs, header names. A consumer must be able to point your widget at any endpoint or database without touching source. Return structured data (dicts, typed objects) rather than formatted strings - let the caller decide how to present it. Do not log to stdout/stderr; raise exceptions or return error values instead.
domain_notes.data: Transformation logic must be pure and stateless - same input always produces same output, no side effects. Accept the broadest practical input type (bytes, str, file-like, path) and let the caller choose. Expose encoding, delimiter, schema, and other format details as parameters. Raise descriptive errors on malformed input rather than silently coercing or dropping data.
domain_notes.ml: Expose model path, endpoint URL, and inference parameters (temperature, max_tokens, thresholds) as arguments - never hardcode them. Return raw model output or a typed result object; do not format or truncate. See language_notes for framework-specific constraints.
domain_notes.security: Never log secrets, tokens, or PII - not even partially. Accept credentials as parameters, never read them from environment variables or files internally. Crypto parameters (key size, algorithm, salt rounds) must be explicit arguments with safe defaults. Fail closed: on any ambiguous input, reject rather than guess.
domain_notes.infra: Accept all paths and hostnames as parameters - never construct paths from hardcoded roots. Config keys, log formats, and health check endpoints must be configurable. Return structured status objects rather than printing; let the caller handle output. Side effects (file writes, process spawns) must be opt-in, not automatic.
domain_notes.frontend: All appearance values (colors, spacing, typography, shadows) must be exposed as parameters or CSS custom properties - hardcoded values lock consumers into your choices. Provide sensible defaults but every visual value must be overridable. No inline styles for anything that could vary by theme.
domain_notes.universal: Use this domain when a widget spans multiple domains or has no clear home — not because it must be pure. A retry utility, a date formatter, a general-purpose HTTP client all belong here. Expose variation points as parameters. Don't force it into a domain just to avoid universal.
domain_notes.modeling: Every dimension and tolerance must be a parameter with a sensible default - never hardcode sizes. Module names must be nouns describing the shape, not verbs. Include a parameter for fit tolerance where physical assembly is involved. All parameters must have comments explaining units (mm, degrees) and valid ranges. Widgets must render cleanly with default parameters - the example must produce a non-empty mesh.
